annotations.title: Aſke in faith nothing doubting.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> The Proteſtants vvould proue by this, that no man ought to pray without aſſurance that he ſhal obtaine that vvhich he aſketh. Where the Apoſtle meaneth nothing els, but that the aſker of lavvful things may not either miſtruſt Gods power and hability, or be in diffidence and deſpaire of his mercie: but that our doubt be onely in our owne vnworthineſſe or vndue aſking.

notes.text: What faith is required in praier.

annotations.title: Let no man ſay that he is tempted of God.
annotations.text: ◦ Vve ſee by this, that when the Scriptures (as in the Pater noſter and other places) ſeeme to ſay, that God doth ſometimes tempt vs, or leade vs into tentation: they meane not, that God is any waies the author, cauſer, or mouer of any man to ſinne, but onely by permiſſion, and becauſe by his gratious povver he keepeth not the offender from tentations. Therfore the blaſphemie of Heretikes, making God the author of ſinne, is intolerable. See S. Auguſt. ſer. 9 de diuerſ. c. 9.

notes.text: God is not author of euil.

annotations.title: God is not a tempter of euils.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> The Proteſtants as much as they may, to diminiſh the force of the Apoſtles concluſion againſt ſuch as attribute their euil tentations to God (for other tentations God doth ſend to trie mens patience and proue their faith) take and tranſlate the vvord paſſiuely, in this ſenſe, that God is not tempted by our euils. Vvhere more conſonantly to the letter and circumſtance of the vvordes before & after, & as agreably <mn>[2]</mn> to the Greeke, it ſhould be taken actiuely as it is in the Latin, that God is no tempter to euil: for being taken paſſiuely, there is no coherence of ſenſe to the other vvordes of the Apoſtle.

annotations.title: Concupiſcence when it hath conceiued.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Concupiſcence (vve ſee here) of it ſelf is not ſinne, as Heretikes falſely teach: but vvhen by any conſent of the minde we do obey or yeld to it, then it is ſinne ingendred and formed in vs.

notes.text: Concupiscence of it self no sinne.

annotations.title: Sinne conſummate ingendreth death.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Here vve ſee that not al ſinne nor al conſent vnto concupiſcence is mortal or damnable, but vvhen it is conſummate, that is, vvhen the conſent of mans minde fully and perfectly yeldeth to the committing or liking of the acte or motion wherevnto concupiſcence moueth or inciteth vs.

annotations.title: The law of perfect libertie.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> The lavv of the Goſpel and grace of Chriſt, is called the law of libertie, in reſpect of the yoke and burden of the old carnal ceremonies, and becauſe Chriſt hath by his bloud of the new Teſtament deliuered all that obey him, from the ſeruitude of ſinne and the Diuel. But not as the Libertines and other Heretikes of this time would haue it, that in the new Teſtament euery man may follow his ovvne liking and conſcience, & may chooſe vvhether he vvil be vnder the lawes and obedience of Spiritual or Temporal Rulers, or no.

notes.text: What is the law of libertie in the New Testament.

annotations.title: Religion cleane.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> True religion ſtandeth not onely in talking of the Scriptures, or onely faith, or Chriſtes iuſtice: but in puritie of life, and good workes, ſpecially of charitie and mercie done by the grace of Chriſt. This is the Apoſtolical doctrine, and far from the Heretical vanitie of this time.

notes.text: Good workes a part of mans iustice.
